To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a supervised approach to retinal vessel segmentation can achieve performance better than the 1st human observer and other methods in the literature, and that the performance can be improved further by using a more sophisticated feature vector.

a 7-dimensional feature vector consisting of morphological, line strength, and multi-scale Gabor filter outputs can effectively classify vessel pixels from non-vessel pixels in ocular fundus retinal images, and that the Gaussian Mixture Classifier is an effective classifier for this purpose.

our proposed methodology is able to achieve a high sensitivity (99.6%), specificity (99.9%) and accuracy (99.8%) for segmentation of the vascular tree in the retinal images of the STARE database, and a high sensitivity (98.6%), specificity(99.8%) and accuracy (98.9%) for segmentation of vascular tree in the DRIVE database.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed supervised method is capable of producing accurate segmentation of the retina and the retinal vasulature in the presence of noise, occlusion and low contrast.
the use of a 7-D feature space for classification of retinal vessels is better than using a 4-D or a 3-D feature space.

a supervised approach can be used for segmentation of the vasculature from retinal images, and that a combination of morphological, line-strength and Gabor features is effective in classifying vessels and non-vessels.
